segments.title: 第123章 青梅之約
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years, Chapter 123: The Childhood Sweetheart's Pact

Actually, Li Luo had also wanted to recommend "Literary Age" to Xu Rongsheng.

But on second thought, recommending just this one book in front of Xu Youyu would seem a little too deliberate.

To be safe, Li Luo played it steady and didn't put his senior on the spot at the dinner table.

After the meal, both the hosts and guests were very pleased.

The parents exchanged phone numbers, saying they could contact each other if anything came up in the future.

"It's a shame Chanxi's dad had something on today and couldn't make it." Li Guohong had a pleasant chat with Xu Rongsheng and said regretfully as they were leaving, "Next time he's free, we parents can get together again."

"No problem, you're always welcome here," Xu Rongsheng said with a cheerful smile.

"If there's a next time, we can't let you go to all this trouble again." Lin Xiuhong said with a smile, "Come to our place then, and let me cook a good meal."

The families then said their goodbyes.

But just as the couple, Xu Rongsheng and Cui Suling, were seeing their guests off, they saw their own daughter heading out with them.

Cui Suling immediately frowned and asked, "Youyu, where are you going?"

"I'm going back," Xu Youyu said, blinking.

"It's rare for you to come home. How can you leave right after lunch?" Cui Suling was exasperated. She quickly reached out and pulled her back. "Stay for one night, go back tomorrow."

"No, I can't," Xu Youyu said, shaking her head repeatedly.

She wasn't a freak like Li Luo, who had an endless supply of stockpiled chapters. She still had to write tonight, alright?

So, Xu Youyu said, "I'll stay until evening. I'll head back after dinner."

"That's fine too. Just don't leave so early. At least keep us company." As Cui Suling said this, she turned to Xu Rongsheng and said, "It's perfect, Li Luo brought some fruit just now. There are some green grapes you like, I'll go wash some."

"He has good taste."

"Isn't it because your daughter egged him on to buy them? She doesn't know how to be polite," Cui Suling said irritably.

"Mom, I didn't! Li Luo picked them all out himself!"

"Why didn't you say so earlier? Now that he's gone, you say this. Anyone can sling mud."

Xu Youyu: "..."

Damn it, Li Luo, you just wait!

After leaving Xu Youyu's home, Li Luo and the others walked out of the residential complex.

A car came to pick up Yuan Wanqing, so she and Yan Zhusheng said goodbye to everyone right at the complex gate.

Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong had also driven over. Since Li Guohong had been drinking at lunch, Lin Xiuhong had to drive back.

Since Ying Zhicheng wasn't going home this week, Ying Chanxi didn't really want to go back either. So, Li Luo walked with her toward Azure Sea Court instead of going home with his parents.

Once it was finally just the two of them, Ying Chanxi's steps became much lighter on the way back.

"Although I tested you once before the exams, I didn't expect you to actually score so high." Ying Chanxi pursed her lips and turned to look at Li Luo's profile. She opened her mouth as if wanting to say something, but the words didn't come out right away.

"It's a pity I couldn't clinch first in the grade," Li Luo shook his head and sighed. "Otherwise, I'd really have loved to hear you woof at the flag-raising ceremony."

"Don't be too arrogant." Ying Chanxi squinted at him, but then she added, "But if you really want to aim for first in the grade, I have a suggestion."

"Hmm?" Li Luo looked at Ying Chanxi, puzzled, wondering what she had in mind.

"Ahem, ahem... it's like this." Ying Chanxi cleared her throat and said with a serious tone and a hint of impartial objectivity, "Although it's very impressive that you could rank in the top thirty of the grade from a parallel class."

"But, at your level, it's hard to find sufficient motivation if you stay in a parallel class."

"And Class One, being the strongest class among the honors classes, if you could transfer over, you'd immediately get into that state of high-intensity studying, surrounded by top students."

"So..."

"So you want me to transfer to Class One?" Li Luo glanced at Ying Chanxi with some surprise, then chuckled. "You want to be in the same class as me that much?"

"N-no, I don't!" Ying Chanxi denied loudly. "I'm just analyzing it from your academic perspective and offering a more suitable plan. Besides, Teacher Sun quite likes you too. You can consider it."

Seeing Ying Chanxi's duplicitous look was quite cute.

However, Li Luo didn't bother to expose her. He just shook his head and said, "Let's forget it. Teacher Kong treats me well, and I've gotten familiar with the students and teachers in my class. There's no need to switch classes at this point."

"Oh, uh... right..." Hearing Li Luo's direct refusal, Ying Chanxi's voice suddenly became sullen. "You have a point."

She didn't insist, but she did harbor some hope, wishing that Li Luo might decisively choose to be in her class for her sake.

If it couldn't happen... it wasn't that big of a deal.

They lived together most of the time anyway.

"Don't overthink it. We'll be regrouped into new classes in the second year anyway," Li Luo said, seeing her dejected mood and offering some comfort.

"That's right!" Ying Chanxi's eyes lit up. "Li Luo, are you choosing liberal arts or sciences?"

"We can both choose the same thing then. With your current scores, you'd probably be placed directly into Class One or Class Sixteen, right?"

"That way, we can be in the same class again."

"Well..." Li Luo blinked, and after some thought, he said to Ying Chanxi, "I heard from Teacher Kong that for our grade, there might be Gaokao reform measures."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback. "What do you mean?"

"I mean the Gaokao system in our province might undergo some changes," Li Luo said. "The specifics haven't been finalized yet, but in the future, it might not be a simple division between liberal arts and sciences, but rather a format of the three main subjects—Chinese, Math, English—plus any three elective minor subjects to form classes."

"For real?" Ying Chanxi's eyes widened, this was the first time she'd ever heard of such a thing. "We can choose any minor subjects?"

"I don't know if we can choose just any, but there will be a more flexible course selection model," Li Luo said. "When they reassign classes, it will definitely be based on everyone's course selections."

"Th-then if it's really like that," Ying Chanxi couldn't help but ask, "what will you choose?"

"Er... ahem." Li Luo gave an embarrassed, dry laugh. "I'll probably still choose the three pure liberal arts subjects."

After all, with the memory palace, liberal arts were definitely much easier to learn than sciences.

For things like physics and chemistry, just memorizing formulas would only get you the basic points.

To get a high score, you needed to be able to apply the various concepts flexibly and achieve true mastery.

The memory palace alone was far from enough for that.

Li Luo was self-aware. He couldn't be sure the Gaokao exam papers wouldn't change due to the butterfly effect he brought about after his rebirth, so it was better to play it safe.

But after hearing Li Luo's words, Ying Chanxi fell silent.

Because according to her original plan, she was supposed to choose sciences.

In that case, regardless of whether the Gaokao system was reformed or not, it seemed unlikely they would be assigned to the same class in their second year.

"Alright, stop overthinking," Li Luo said, rubbing Ying Chanxi's head vigorously. "There's still so much time. It's useless to think too much."

"Then I can choose liberal arts too." Ying Chanxi shook her head, patting Li Luo's hand away. "It doesn't make a huge difference anyway. I'm just aiming for Qianjiang University."

"You originally wanted to choose sciences, right?" Li Luo glanced at her.

Li Luo vaguely remembered that in his past life, Ying Chanxi had gotten into the computer science department at Qianjiang University.

It seemed to be a major related to image processing and video production.

Generally speaking, pure liberal arts students couldn't choose that kind of major.

But Ying Chanxi said, "I'll choose whatever I want to choose."

"You really are stubborn." Li Luo flicked her forehead lightly and then sighed helplessly. "When the time comes, just tell me what you want to choose, and I'll choose the same thing as you."

It would just take a bit more effort... he was planning on being a little lazy, but it looked like that wouldn't be possible now.

"Really?" Ying Chanxi's eyes brightened.

"Really."

"But..." Ying Chanxi bit her lip, hesitating again. "You prefer..."

"No buts," Li Luo interrupted. "I just think liberal arts are less strenuous to study. If I end up choosing sciences, you'll have to be responsible for me. If you can't teach me well, I'll blame you."

"No problem!" Hearing him say that, Ying Chanxi instantly breathed a sigh of relief, then happily patted her chest. "Leave it to me."

After this private conversation with Li Luo and the promise they made to each other, Ying Chanxi's originally somewhat blue mood immediately turned sunny and bright.

(End of Chapter)
